title: Best ISP Tracking & DNS Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare VPNs and encrypted DNS services that limit what your internet provider can see, scored on one published rubric.
intro: Your internet provider can see every website you visit, sell your browsing data, and throttle your connection. These tools help you reclaim your privacy by encrypting DNS queries, masking your traffic, and preventing ISP surveillance.

verdict.summary: A VPN hides the most from your ISP because it encrypts all your traffic, not just DNS lookups. On these five criteria ExpressVPN and NordVPN tie for the top score; ExpressVPN is listed first only because ties are ordered alphabetically. NordVPN is rated higher for malware blocking, and ExpressVPN for ease of setup. If you only want to hide your DNS lookups, Quad9 and Cloudflare are free; Quad9 scores higher because it blocks malicious domains by default, while Cloudflare blocks malware only on its separate 1.1.1.2 resolver. Encrypted DNS alone still leaves the IP addresses you connect to and your traffic volume visible to your ISP. Speed isn't scored, because we haven't measured it.

pro_tips: Combine a VPN with encrypted DNS for maximum ISP protection - use your VPN's DNS servers when connected and a service like Cloudflare when not
Test your DNS privacy at dnsleaktest.com to ensure your ISP can't see your DNS queries
Enable DNS over HTTPS in your browser settings (Chrome, Firefox) for an extra layer of DNS encryption
On Android 9 or later, set Private DNS to a provider hostname such as one.one.one.one or dns.quad9.net to encrypt DNS lookups for every app on the phone
Check if your ISP offers opt-out options for data collection, though technical solutions are more reliable than policy promises

faqs.question: Can my ISP see what websites I visit with encrypted DNS?
faqs.answer: With encrypted DNS alone, your ISP can't see specific websites, but they can still see the IP addresses you connect to and estimate your activity. For complete protection, combine encrypted DNS with a VPN.

faqs.question: Is changing DNS settings enough to stop ISP tracking?
faqs.answer: Changing to encrypted DNS helps but isn't complete protection. Your ISP can still see traffic patterns, connection times, and data volumes. A VPN provides more comprehensive protection by encrypting all your traffic.

faqs.question: Do free DNS services like Cloudflare really protect my privacy?
faqs.answer: They protect your DNS lookups from your ISP, and reputable services publish privacy commitments: Cloudflare says it never writes your IP address to disk and deletes query logs within 25 hours, and Quad9 says it doesn't record IP addresses. They only protect DNS queries, though; your ISP can still see the IP addresses you connect to and how much data you use.

faqs.question: Will using a VPN slow down my internet significantly?
faqs.answer: A VPN adds some slowdown because your traffic takes an extra hop and is encrypted. How much depends on the server's distance and load; choosing a nearby server and a modern protocol such as WireGuard, NordLynx or Lightway keeps it small for most uses.

faqs.question: Can I use multiple privacy tools together?
faqs.answer: Yes, combining tools often increases protection. For example, use encrypted DNS all the time and turn on a VPN for sensitive activities. When the VPN is on, let it handle DNS so the two settings don't conflict.
